When it is decided: once in each stage of the dispute; paid 30 days after the stage begins
Decision date: P5 15 May 2024, median 15 May 2024, P95 15 May 2024 = when the decision falls, across the simulations that reach it

Projected available cash at decision date: P5 $11.6M, median $11.6M = opening cash + projected operating flows from the bank data + the dispute's cash to that date, across the simulations that reach the decision
Amount owed at decision: median $0, highest $0 = the judgment on this path (as entered, or as the ruling leaves it) + statutory interest to the decision date - amounts already collected

Settlement offer: P5 $5.9M, median $6.1M = the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed (30-day need: median $2.8M); paid as 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date (30 days after the decision) and one each month after; the claim is released on the settlement date; installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall after the analysis period
The notes' interest payment date: 17 Jun 2024: $1,320,000.00 due, paid in shares
Nasdaq's deadline to regain compliance with the minimum bid price: 21 Oct 2024

On the loan: through the company's cash. Slope debits each installment in full on its due date when the company's available cash covers it; a debit that fails stays past due and is retried on the next due date or month-end. Slope funds a draw only while nothing is overdue and no petition is filed

However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.

quotes.quote: Having acquired the Asserted Trade Secrets by improper means, Akoustis used the Asserted Trade Secrets as a shortcut to competing in the market. In particular, the Asserted Trade Secrets resulted in a 55-month head start benefit for Akoustis.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by at least $66.1 million as a result of its 55- month head start.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 41. An injunction is warranted to enjoin Akoustis from falsely promoting polycrystalline products as “single crystal.” 42. Qorvo is also owed damages of $1,146,604 for corrective advertising that addresses Akoustis’s false claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 49. Qorvo is owed damages of $809,772 for the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees.

quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.

quotes.quote: Having acquired the Asserted Trade Secrets by improper means, Akoustis used the Asserted Trade Secrets as a shortcut to competing in the market. In particular, the Asserted Trade Secrets resulted in a 55-month head start benefit for Akoustis.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by at least $66.1 million as a result of its 55- month head start.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 41. An injunction is warranted to enjoin Akoustis from falsely promoting polycrystalline products as “single crystal.” 42. Qorvo is also owed damages of $1,146,604 for corrective advertising that addresses Akoustis’s false claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 49. Qorvo is owed damages of $809,772 for the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 50. Qorvo is owed $66.1 million, representing the amount by which Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by its unfair and deceptive trade practices.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 19. Qorvo is owed damages of $279,808 for Akoustis’ infringement of the ’755 and ’018 Patents for the period of October 5, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order denying the motions to exclude the opinions of Carolyn Irwin and Melissa Bennis (D.I. 553)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s motion for summary judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, Qorvo’s motion for partial summary judgment with respect to the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent was granted. The trial with respect to the Delaware Proceeding commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: That same day, Qorvo filed a motion seeking partial summary judgment in its favor with respect to the Company’s defenses of invalidity regarding the ’018 Patent and the ’755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. Revenue, however, is not a cognizable basis for calculating unjust enrichment except as part of the calculation of a defendant’s “ill-gotten” profits – something that Ms. Bennis does not purport to calculate, as Akoustis has never earned a profit.

quotes.quote: Having acquired the Asserted Trade Secrets by improper means, Akoustis used the Asserted Trade Secrets as a shortcut to competing in the market. In particular, the Asserted Trade Secrets resulted in a 55-month head start benefit for Akoustis.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by at least $66.1 million as a result of its 55- month head start.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 41. An injunction is warranted to enjoin Akoustis from falsely promoting polycrystalline products as “single crystal.” 42. Qorvo is also owed damages of $1,146,604 for corrective advertising that addresses Akoustis’s false claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 49. Qorvo is owed damages of $809,772 for the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 50. Qorvo is owed $66.1 million, representing the amount by which Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by its unfair and deceptive trade practices.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 19. Qorvo is owed damages of $279,808 for Akoustis’ infringement of the ’755 and ’018 Patents for the period of October 5, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order denying the motions to exclude the opinions of Carolyn Irwin and Melissa Bennis (D.I. 553)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s motion for summary judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, Qorvo’s motion for partial summary judgment with respect to the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent was granted. The trial with respect to the Delaware Proceeding commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: That same day, Qorvo filed a motion seeking partial summary judgment in its favor with respect to the Company’s defenses of invalidity regarding the ’018 Patent and the ’755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Unjust enrichment for trade secret misappropriation under a “head -start” theory in the amount of $66.1 million;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. Revenue, however, is not a cognizable basis for calculating unjust enrichment except as part of the calculation of a defendant’s “ill-gotten” profits – something that Ms. Bennis does not purport to calculate, as Akoustis has never earned a profit.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: Having acquired the Asserted Trade Secrets by improper means, Akoustis used the Asserted Trade Secrets as a shortcut to competing in the market. In particular, the Asserted Trade Secrets resulted in a 55-month head start benefit for Akoustis.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by at least $66.1 million as a result of its 55- month head start.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 41. An injunction is warranted to enjoin Akoustis from falsely promoting polycrystalline products as “single crystal.” 42. Qorvo is also owed damages of $1,146,604 for corrective advertising that addresses Akoustis’s false claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 49. Qorvo is owed damages of $809,772 for the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 50. Qorvo is owed $66.1 million, representing the amount by which Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by its unfair and deceptive trade practices.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 19. Qorvo is owed damages of $279,808 for Akoustis’ infringement of the ’755 and ’018 Patents for the period of October 5, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order denying the motions to exclude the opinions of Carolyn Irwin and Melissa Bennis (D.I. 553)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: State the amount Akoustis was unjustly enriched by misappropriating Qorvo’s trade secrets as to which you have answered “Yes” and “Yes” in Question 1(a) above.

quotes.quote: What do you find is the amount of damages, if any, that should be paid to Qorvo for the infringement of each Asserted Patent, to compensate for the damages caused by Akoustis’ infringement?

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s motion for summary judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, Qorvo’s motion for partial summary judgment with respect to the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent was granted. The trial with respect to the Delaware Proceeding commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: That same day, Qorvo filed a motion seeking partial summary judgment in its favor with respect to the Company’s defenses of invalidity regarding the ’018 Patent and the ’755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Unjust enrichment for trade secret misappropriation under a “head -start” theory in the amount of $66.1 million;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. Revenue, however, is not a cognizable basis for calculating unjust enrichment except as part of the calculation of a defendant’s “ill-gotten” profits – something that Ms. Bennis does not purport to calculate, as Akoustis has never earned a profit.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: Having acquired the Asserted Trade Secrets by improper means, Akoustis used the Asserted Trade Secrets as a shortcut to competing in the market. In particular, the Asserted Trade Secrets resulted in a 55-month head start benefit for Akoustis.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by at least $66.1 million as a result of its 55- month head start.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: The misappropriation in that case was willful and malicious. Akoustis has undertaken intentional acts to steal Qorvo’s trade secrets and use those trade secrets with reckless indifference to Qorvo’s rights. As a result, Qorvo is entitled to enhanced damages under both the DTSA and the NCTSPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 41. An injunction is warranted to enjoin Akoustis from falsely promoting polycrystalline products as “single crystal.” 42. Qorvo is also owed damages of $1,146,604 for corrective advertising that addresses Akoustis’s false claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 49. Qorvo is owed damages of $809,772 for the cost to recruit, hire, and train additional employees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 50. Qorvo is owed $66.1 million, representing the amount by which Akoustis has been unjustly enriched by its unfair and deceptive trade practices.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 19. Qorvo is owed damages of $279,808 for Akoustis’ infringement of the ’755 and ’018 Patents for the period of October 5, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order denying the motions to exclude the opinions of Carolyn Irwin and Melissa Bennis (D.I. 553)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s motion for summary judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, Qorvo’s motion for partial summary judgment with respect to the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent was granted. The trial with respect to the Delaware Proceeding commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: That same day, Qorvo filed a motion seeking partial summary judgment in its favor with respect to the Company’s defenses of invalidity regarding the ’018 Patent and the ’755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Unjust enrichment for trade secret misappropriation under a “head -start” theory in the amount of $66.1 million;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. Revenue, however, is not a cognizable basis for calculating unjust enrichment except as part of the calculation of a defendant’s “ill-gotten” profits – something that Ms. Bennis does not purport to calculate, as Akoustis has never earned a profit.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: 56. Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.

quotes.quote: 19. Qorvo is owed damages of $279,808 for Akoustis’ infringement of the ’755 and ’018 Patents for the period of October 5, 2021 through June 30, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: Since obtaining knowledge of the ’018 Patent, Akoustis’s infringement has been willful, deliberate, and intentional, and Akoustis is acting in reckless disregard of Qorvo’s patent rights, entitling Qorvo to treble damages.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 62. In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: 28. Akoustis intends to prove that Qorvo is barred from recovering on its claims for trade secret misappropriation because of the three year statute of limitations governing these claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Exhibits to the proposed final pretrial order, including the parties' statements of intended proof (D.I. 543-1)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Plaintiff’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Carolyn Irwin is DENIED. Defendants’ Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on “Head- Start” Damages is DENIED. Defendant’s Motion to Exclude the Testimony of Melissa Bennis on poaching damages will be addressed by separate order, and Parties are ORDERED to submit supplemental briefing as detailed below.

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: 5,000,000 of the Shares (the “Note Shares”) represent shares that may be issued, at our election, as payment of accrued interest on our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”), as make-whole payments made in connection with certain conversions of the Notes or as payments made in connection with qualifying fundamental changes of Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”)

quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.

quotes.quote:
29. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo entitled to any damages for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

30. Akoustis intends to refute that Akoustis’ alleged misappropriation of trade secrets was willful and malicious.

31. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to any injunctive relief for the alleged trade secret misappropriation.

32. Akoustis intends to refute that Qorvo is entitled to attorneys’ fees, costs, pre- judgment interest, or post-judgment interest, or any relief.

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: Unjust enrichment for trade secret misappropriation under a “head -start” theory in the amount of $66.1 million;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: First, it is based on a comparison of the “time value” of bare revenue that Akoustis actually received versus the revenue it allegedly would have received if that revenue had been delayed by 55 months. Revenue, however, is not a cognizable basis for calculating unjust enrichment except as part of the calculation of a defendant’s “ill-gotten” profits – something that Ms. Bennis does not purport to calculate, as Akoustis has never earned a profit.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: For the reasons discussed below, Defendants’ 50(a) motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. There is sufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury for the purpose of liability under the UDTPA, but insufficient evidence to support any compensable damages under the UDTPA.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote:
The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

IT IS SO ORDERED, this 14th day of May, 2024.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Notes: principal: $44.0M; judgment default: final judgments for the payment of money above $10,000,000 that "remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for a period (during which execution shall not be effectively stayed) of 60 days" (§7.01(i)), after notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of the notes
When it is decided: once in each stage of the dispute; paid 30 days after the stage begins
Decision date: P5 17 May 2024, median 21 May 2024, P95 23 May 2024 = when the decision falls, across the simulations that reach it

Projected available cash at decision date: P5 $10.4M, median $11.7M = opening cash + projected operating flows from the bank data + the dispute's cash to that date, across the simulations that reach the decision
Amount owed at decision: median $1.4M, highest $1.4M = the judgment on this path (as entered, or as the ruling leaves it) + statutory interest to the decision date - amounts already collected

Settlement offer: P5 $1.4M, median $1.4M = the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed (30-day need: median $2.8M); paid as 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date (30 days after the decision) and one each month after; the claim is released on the settlement date; installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall after the analysis period
The deadline to file a notice of appeal: between 25 Aug 2024 and 8 Nov 2024 (median 3 Oct 2024)
The notes' interest payment date: 17 Jun 2024: $1,320,000.00 due, paid in shares
Nasdaq's deadline to regain compliance with the minimum bid price: 21 Oct 2024

On the loan: through the company's cash. Slope debits each installment in full on its due date when the company's available cash covers it; a debit that fails stays past due and is retried on the next due date or month-end. Slope funds a draw only while nothing is overdue and no petition is filed

nodes.question: Does the judgment debtor move for a stay on a bond or other security?
nodes.context: before the ruling
nodes.label: Akoustis moves for stay
nodes.sub: Before ruling · without principal measure

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

steps.text: 28 U.S.C. §1963: a judgment may be registered in another district "when the judgment has become final by appeal or expiration of the time for appeal or when ordered by the court that entered the judgment for good cause shown." Good cause: thin forum assets and substantial assets elsewhere (Associated Bus. Tel. Sys. v. Greater Capital Corp., 128 F.R.D. 63, 66-68 (D.N.J. 1989)).

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(a): "execution on a judgment and proceedings to enforce it are stayed for 30 days after its entry, unless the court orders otherwise."
Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.
11 U.S.C. §362(a): a bankruptcy petition operates as a stay of any act to collect a claim against the debtor that arose before the petition.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

nodes.question: Do three or more noteholders file an involuntary bankruptcy petition against the issuer?

nodes.label: Holders file after no-action period

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b); JMOL only where the record lacks the minimum evidence to support the verdict (Lightning Lube v. Witco, 4 F.3d 1153, 1166 (3d Cir. 1993)).

Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

Remittitur is to the maximum the evidence supports, and the plaintiff may refuse it and take a new trial (Hetzel v. Prince William County, 523 U.S. 208 (1998); Kazan v. Wolinski, 721 F.2d 911 (3d Cir. 1983)).

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

nodes.question: Do three or more noteholders file an involuntary bankruptcy petition against the issuer?
nodes.context: after acceleration on the delisting (suspended without a hearing)
nodes.label: Holders file after no-action period
nodes.sub: Delisting · suspended, no hearing · set aside

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.
